faq.q: How does weight help a motorbike lean?
faq.a: When the bike leans, its weight acts through a point to the side of where the tyres touch the road. That gives a turning effect into the bend, which balances the tipping effect of the tyre grip.
asks: Why doesn't a leaning motorbike fall over?

faq.q: Does the road push up on a leaning motorbike?
faq.a: Yes. The road pushes up with a force equal to the weight of bike and rider. Together with the sideways grip, it makes a combined push that points along the line of the leaning bike.
asks: What holds a motorbike up in a turn?

faq.q: What force turns a motorbike round a bend?
faq.a: Friction between the tyres and the road pushes the bike towards the centre of the turn. A force pointing to the centre of a curve is called a centripetal force.

faq.q: How do riders start a lean?
faq.a: Riders briefly push the handlebar on the side they want to turn, called countersteering. Pushing the left bar forward steers the front wheel right for a moment, so the bike tips left into the turn.

faq.q: Why do racing bikes lean so far?
faq.a: At high speed in tight bends they need a very big sideways grip force, so they must lean further to balance it. MotoGP riders lean beyond 60 degrees.
asks: How far can a motorbike lean?

facts: MotoGP riders can lean their bikes more than 60 degrees from upright.
The sideways force that turns a motorbike comes from tyre grip on the road.
Riders start a lean by countersteering: briefly pushing the handlebar on the side they want to turn.

quiz.say: What provides the force that turns a motorbike round a bend?
quiz.show: What provides the force that turns a motorbike round a bend?
quiz.why: Friction between tyres and road pushes the bike towards the centre of the turn.

wrong.1: The engine drives the bike forward; it does not push it sideways.
wrong.2: Air resistance acts backwards against the motion, not towards the bend.
